newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary K&H bank pays 10pct div. on pref. shares.
newsitem.headline: Hungary K&H bank pays 10pct div. on pref. shares.

text.p: Hungary's Kereskedelmi es Hitelbank Rt (K&H) shareholders approved on Thursday a 10 percent dividend on preference shares on 1996 earnings but the management said it was not considering payments for the previous years.

"The management does not plan retroactive dividend payment, but will reconsider the issue annually in the light of the results," Andras Szentgyorgyi, the bank's legal adviser, told shareholders at the bank's annual general meeting.
Instead, owners of preference shares will have voting rights until the bank pays dividends for the years from 1993 to 1995, Szentgyorgyi said.
Preference shares represent some two percent of the bank's 10.38 billion forints issued share capital. The owners of ordinary shares will not receive a dividend on 1996 earnings.
General Manager Janos Eros said the merger into K&H of its former unit IBUSZ Bank on January 1, 1996, gave the bank the second biggest branch network in the country.
He also said that last year K&H had the largest selection of bank cards on offer, including two co-branded cards, one with retail group Fotex Rt and another with retailer Centrum Aruhazak RT.
K&H plans to launch a forint credit card in the second half of this year, the first such card in Hungary, the bank said in its 1997 business plan.
It also said that lending to large and medium-size businesses will remain the bank's main strategic goal.
"We still regard the financing of small enterprises as risky and do not plan a significant increase of these clients or loans and products related to them," the bank said.
Eros said the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development's $30 million subordinated loan increased confidence in K&H and improved its privatisation prospects.
Privatisation agency APV Rt said last month it had chosen the Bank of Ireland and a consortium of Belgium's Kredietbank and Irish Life as final bidders for K&H.
Hungary said it would sell a stake of at least 25 percent plus one vote in K&H to a strategic investor who may invite a partner to raise the bank's equity by at least $30 million.
The deadline for the final tender is July 10.
K&H's 1996 consolidated balance sheet total was 363.9 billion forints, up 6.3 percent on 1995, while its net profit was 2.396 billion forints, 8.5 percent higher than in 1995.
On Hungary's OTC (over-the-counter) market K&H preference shares were offered on Thursday between 185 and 210 percent of their nominal value, while bids ranged from 115 to 140 percent.
Oridnary K&H shares were offered at between 230 and 250 percent while bids ranged from 170 to 210 percent.
